honey-yellow.$description: Honey Yellow — Yellow wash for highlight backgrounds, decorative bands, and soft emphasis behind content.

marigold.$description: Marigold — Accent fills on cards, headline underline strokes, icon highlights, secondary callouts — slightly punchier sibling of Honey Yellow for moments that need to sit on white

inkwell.$description: Inkwell — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

carbon.$description: Carbon — Body text and high-contrast borders on light surfaces, alt dark fill for emphasis blocks

slate-gray.$description: Slate Gray — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

pebble.$description: Pebble — Muted helper text, secondary metadata, low-emphasis captions

river-mist.$description: River Mist — Card and link borders on white surfaces, hairline dividers — cool enough to feel distinct from the warm yellow system

fog.$description: Fog — Subtle borders, disabled state outlines, very light separators

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page and card surfaces, text on dark fills, primary button text

stk-bureau-serif.$description: Display and large headline face — the editorial voice for hero statements, section titles, and feature headlines. Tight tracking (-0.027em to -0.05em) pulls the letters into a dense, magazine-like block. A serif in a SaaS hero is the signature move; it humanizes the product and signals 'crafted for creatives'.

stk-bureau-sans.$description: Workhorse UI and body face — navigation, buttons, paragraphs, form fields, cards. Weights 500–700 handle subheads and CTAs. The pairing with the serif display creates a clear voice hierarchy: serif for poetry, sans for instructions.

stk-gerhard.$description: Tiny all-caps eyebrow labels above section headers (e.g. 'CAPTURE LEADS') — wide tracking (+0.071em) in uppercase gives every section a labeled, editorial entry point. Used sparingly; one per section, never in body copy.
